title: PR merge risk matrix & quick mitigations
content:
Goal: produce a compact, actionable checklist + risk matrix for small-to-medium PRs that touch runtime scheduling, KV cache, or batching heuristics. Use this as my personal quick-reference during reviews and to seed reviewer comments.

Summary notes:
- Keep this intentionally short — 1–2 mins per PR for low-risk, 5–10 mins for medium, escalate for high-risk.
- Focus areas: correctness guarantees, perf regressions, observability, and safe rollback.
- Prefer explicit instrumentation hooks over 'trust me' changes (add tracing spans or debug metrics).

Risk matrix (quick):
- Low risk: docs, small refactors without behavior changes, UI tweaks to dashboard.
- Medium risk: perf-related changes (batching, loop shifts), retries/backoff adjustments, additional caching logic with new invalidation edges.
- High risk: model execution path changes, KV cache format changes, network protocol/schema changes, migration scripts, or anything that touches on customer data path.

Checklist (fast pass) — tick off in review comments:
1) API compatibility: does the change alter request/response schema or opt-in flags? If yes, is there a migration plan? (look for feature gates, config defaults)
2) Observability: are new code paths instrumented with metrics/logs/traces? Add a one-liner to the PR if not.
3) Tests: unit tests + integration test targets. For perf changes, is there a microbenchmark or load test recorded (link to artifacts)?
4) Safety nets: are there canary flags, circuit breakers, fallbacks? If a fast path is added, is there an automatic revert condition?
5) Rollback: can this be rolled back with a config flip or requires DB/migration reversal? Note the expected rollback steps.
6) Cost/regression estimate: does this increase GPU/CPU usage or token spend? Add rough estimate.
7) Security/data: any PII handling or KMS/HSM interactions? Add approver if yes.
8) Code clarity & invariants: do core invariants have assertions? Are boundary conditions covered?

Rapid heuristics (how I triage):
- If change touches "batcher" or "scheduler" files AND size > 300 LOC => treat as medium-to-high; ask for perf bench.
- If a change introduces a new serialized format (any class named *Proto*/marshal) => high risk; require migration note + compatibility tests.
- If change removes telemetry or changes sampling rates => medium risk; request monitoring dashboard updates.

Common PR red flags to call out immediately:
- TODOs left in core loop ("TODO: handle X"), especially without ticket reference.
- Silent retries with exponential backoff but no max retry cap.
- Hidden feature flags (config flags without README/docs).
- Changes to cache invalidation touching more than one service boundary.

Mitigations to suggest in comments (boilerplate I paste):
- "Please add a lightweight integration test that simulates X and asserts Y. If adding load tests, include artifact link in PR description."
- "Add a trace/span around the new fast-path with tag=feature_X so we can filter in tracing UI for 1st 24h post-merge."
- "Can we gate this behind an opt-in config default=false? If not feasible, document rollback steps in the PR description."
- "If this changes memory allocation pattern, please include estimated delta and a simple smoke benchmark script in dev/bench/*."

Refactor/Follow-up ideas (logged here so I remember later):
- Consolidate batching heuristics: a single policy object + policy registry rather than multiple if/else scattered in scheduler.* files. Ticket idea: SERV-1198.
- Extract a thin compatibility shim layer for KV cache format so we avoid coupling migration logic into runtime startup.
- Add a lightweight chaos test that randomly drops KV cache responses to validate graceful fallback behavior (run in staging CI).

Post-merge quick actions (what I or SRE will do after merging risky change):
- Create a dedicated dashboard tile that tracks the new metric + alert threshold for 24–72h.
- Schedule a 1h smoke-check with the oncall to manually validate tail latencies.
- Keep a short rollback playbook in the PR thread with exact commands (kubectl patch/scale / feature flag toggle).

Unresolved questions to follow up in review thread:
- "Is this change expected to create more partial responses in streaming paths?"
- "If an instance fails during model compile, what fallback path is exercised?"
- "Will the new path increase peak GPU memory usage? Have we measured OOM probability on p3/gnode?"

Notes-to-self for future reviewer templates:
- Insert a one-paragraph REQUIRED "What could go wrong" section in PR descriptions for any change labeled servicing/runtime.
- Keep an up-to-date list of 'safe revert commands' in the SRE playbook and link it in PR template.

Quick personal TODOs (small, actionable):
- Add the one-paragraph PR template suggestion to repo PR template (small docs change).
- Draft a short internal postmortem template for runtime regressions that includes the above metrics and rollback timeline.

Examples to reference when commenting:
- Good: PR #1972 had a clear rollback flag and a canary script attached — model for future comments.
- Bad: PR #1888 changed cache key structure inline with no migration tests — caused a 2hr incident.

End state: keep this doc as a dynamic, minimal checklist. Copy snippets into PR comments as needed and iterate whenever we hit a new incident or pattern.

---
Local scratch: drop quick paste templates below when I'm reviewing:
- "Observed risk: [low|medium|high] — justification: <one sentence>. Suggested mitigation: <one line>. Required reviewer: @eng-lead or @sre-oncall if high."
- "Rollback steps: 1) toggle feature flag X 2) scale down deployment Y to Z 3) revert PR and redeploy. Estimated time to recover: ~N minutes."
